architecture.tabModel: One global workspace tab strip. Every browser page, file, PDF, spreadsheet, Terminal, Files, Git, Usage, and Notes surface is a peer tab; there is no nested browser tab strip.

browserResidency.policy: true LRU with the active page protected; evicted pages retain bounded resume metadata and remount on user or agent activation

architecture.manualProcessObservation: Nine browser pages were present as tab metadata while the packaged app retained four browser renderer processes plus the main renderer. The observed live set remained below the six-page ordinary ceiling instead of retaining one renderer per metadata tab.

tests.title: Y Space identity and compatibility migration
evidence: The packaged app launched as Y Space against the existing profile.
Existing project, task, tool, and browser-page metadata restored.
Compatibility-sensitive data paths and partitions remain stable; migration tests pass.

tests.title: Browser pages are independent global workspace tabs
evidence: The sole top tab strip showed independent Alpha, Gamma, and DuckDuckGo browser pages beside Files and document tabs.
Cmd+T created a new browser page as a peer global tab; no nested browser strip appeared.
Switching pages preserved Gamma's Network request verified state.
Cmd+W inside a browser guest closed that browser page and selected the adjacent Files peer tab.

tests.title: Codex controls and reuses embedded browser pages
evidence: Codex listed the exact Y Space browser-page inventory and active page.
It found Alpha, activated it, filled and saved Controlled by Codex through Y Space, and observed the confirmation.
It focused the existing Gamma URL without duplication, ran the request, observed Network request verified, and captured a Browser screenshot.
No external browser was used.

tests.title: Claude Code embedded-browser access
evidence: Claude Code 2.1.210 is installed.
claude auth status reported loggedIn=false, authMethod=none, apiProvider=firstParty.

tests.title: OpenCode models and packaged embedded-browser control
evidence: OpenCode 1.18.23 reported configured OpenCode Zen and Z.AI providers.
opencode/gpt-5.6-luna returned YSPACE_OPENCODE_GPT_PASS.
zai/glm-4.5-flash returned YSPACE_OPENCODE_GLM_PASS.

It created or focused https://example.com without external browser control and reported active tab tab-3e5ee0a7-e49e-4224-ade6-3229ba824a63 with title Example Domain.
It captured a 39,346-byte 1140x1646 Browser screenshot and returned to Idle.
Signed provider-session isolation and Browser/app-controls wiring pass automated tests.

tests.title: Browser capability, app controls, and Y Space core skills
evidence: Provider launch tests verify Browser and app-controls injection with signed task identity.
Global Browser disable and core-skill synchronization are covered without replacing user-owned skill collisions.
The live Codex run proved the packaged Browser capability is discoverable and operable.

tests.title: Pair Chrome and Brave cookie-import sources
tests.reason: The user explicitly said not to install Chrome or Brave extensions because normal browsing is embedded in Y Space. Import-only bridge security and protocol behavior remain covered by automated tests.

tests.title: Extension-free cookie-file preview and import
evidence: The final packaged app selected a harmless JSON fixture through the native file picker.
The preview and import completed with 1 cookie accepted and 0 rejected for example.com.
No Chrome or Brave extension and no external browser control were used.

tests.title: Cookie-import denial, limits, and legacy-control rejection
evidence: Automated bridge tests cover signed pairing, encryption, malformed P-256 points, expiry, revocation, bounds, redaction, and rejection of legacy browser-control messages.
Manual cookie-file import exercised the extension-free path; external extension pairing remained intentionally uninstalled.

tests.title: Personal Pipedream MCP OAuth
evidence: The implementation and automated tests are present.
tests.reason: A live run would create an OAuth grant/account connection, which was not separately authorized.

tests.title: Packaged Pipedream environment-file safety flow
evidence: The native picker accepted a harmless syntactically complete environment fixture in the final packaged app.
The fake credentials were rejected safely without leaking their values.
Forget environment file removed the saved path and returned the UI to its unconfigured state.
tests.notRun: No real client-credentials token exchange, OAuth grant, or Pipedream account connection was created because that consequential action requires separate authorization.

tests.title: Pipedream disable, disconnect, and restart cleanup
tests.reason: Live teardown requires first creating an authorized account connection; relay, reconciliation, revocation, and restart behavior are covered by automated suites.

tests.title: Pipedream relay spoofing and consequential retry safety
evidence: Tests cover launch bearer enforcement, pinned routing headers, session-to-binding isolation, safe read retry after 401, and no tools/call replay.

tests.title: Secret inheritance and persistence audit
evidence: .env.pipedream is ignored by git and mode 600.
Only required variable names and presence were inspected; values were never printed.
Provider translation and persistence tests verify opaque descriptors, loopback-only bearer exposure, and renderer-safe redaction.

tests.title: Global right-workspace tool tabs
evidence: Files, Git, Usage, Notes, Browser, and Terminal opened or focused as labeled peer tabs in the one global strip.
Top-right Browser focused an existing browser page instead of creating a nested or duplicate tab.

tests.title: Source, Markdown, PDF, XLS, and XLSX global document tabs
evidence: Source and Markdown files opened as peer global tabs.
XLS and XLSX rendered locally with People and Metrics sheets and expected Ada/Grace cells.
The two-page PDF rendered inside the packaged app through Chromium's PDF viewer with 1 / 2 page state and Finished loading PDF.
Malformed XLSX produced a finite in-app error instead of crashing.

tests.title: Mixed-tab reorder, keyboard access, and shortcut isolation
evidence: Mixed browser, document, and tool peers reordered in the sole global strip.
Ctrl+Tab cycled between browser peers and crossed from the last browser page into Files, even with the browser address field focused.
Browser Cmd+T and guest Cmd+W applied to browser peers without invoking a hidden file/editor layer.

tests.title: Agent browser control survives global workspace switching and LRU suspension
evidence: Browser metadata remained discoverable while Files, documents, Git, Usage, and Notes were active.
Agent targeting promotes a suspended page to the resident LRU set before interaction.
Nine browser metadata tabs produced only four browser renderer processes plus the main renderer during packaged QA, below the configured six-page ordinary ceiling.
Automated tests cover LRU promotion/eviction, late-snapshot merge, persistent script/style restoration, sensitive auth redaction, and listener teardown.
